author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing shows the first page when asked for a page before the first
summary: A request for the owner listing at a page below the first is answered with the first page of matches, not an error page.
acceptance_criteria: given an owner listing asked for at a page before the first, when it runs, then the first page of matches is shown and no error page appears
given an owner listing asked for at a page before the first, when it runs, then the paging position shown to the reader is the first page
edge case 4: a page asked for below zero is treated the same as a page of zero - both give the first page
edge case 5: asking for the page before the first while searching by last name keeps that search applied to the first page
non_goals: a page value that is not a number - the owner scoped the report to values below 1
a page beyond the last page of matches - unchanged by this slice
the veterinarian directory's paging - the owner named the owner listing only
notes: Reported reproduction: opening the owner listing at page 0 renders the error page. Owner statement quoted at intake-decision line 1; decisions were empty, so scope is bounded by the request as stated - values below the first page, owner listing only. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Non-numeric and beyond-last-page values stay open questions; raise a consultation-request if implementation needs them.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: No new design ground. The slice is a boundary-normalization fix inside an existing contract: system-design.md#contracts already names OwnerController as the owner search-with-paging surface, and security-principles.md#trust-boundaries already rules that external input is validated for range before use. The defect is that the page request parameter reaches PageRequest.of unchecked at OwnerController.java:135, so a value below 1 yields a negative page index. Clamping it is the control the boundary rule already prescribes; no new pattern, module, or dependency. Resolution basis: read of OwnerController.java lines 94-137 plus grep for PageRequest across owner and vet packages (IDE oracle not connected, so this is the weaker basis).
integration_points: OwnerController.processFindForm receives the page request parameter (default 1) and passes it to two places: findPaginatedForOwnersLastName for the query, and addPaginationModel for the currentPage model attribute the ownersList template renders
OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith is unchanged - it receives a Pageable that is already valid

patterns.description: the @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") page parameter is the single entry point for the value; normalize once there, so the query and the rendered paging position agree
MockMvc controller test seam already exercises /owners with query parameters and asserts model attributes - the four named tests fit this shape with no new test infrastructure

risks.risk: Clamping inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName only. The query would return the first page but addPaginationModel would still put the raw value into currentPage, so the reader is shown a paging position of 0 or negative and the second acceptance criterion fails.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the handler boundary, before both the query call and the model call, so a single value flows onward (security-principles.md#trust-boundaries: external input is validated for range before use, and internal code past the boundary trusts its contracts).

risks.risk: Treating the clamp as a business rule and growing the controller's rule surface.
risks.mitigation: This is request normalization at the HTTP adapter, not a domain rule - it stays in the controller and nothing is added to the domain (architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller row: binds the request, delegates, selects the response, holds no business rule; the recorded controller-rules deviation does not extend to new rules).

risks.risk: Scope drift into VetController, which carries the same page - 1 shape at VetController.java:61.
risks.mitigation: The vet directory's paging is a recorded non_goal for this slice. Leave it untouched; it is a candidate for a later slice, not this one.

notes: docs/system-design.md updated in this dispatch: REQ-OWN-005 added to the OwnerController Contracts row, and the row's Purpose now names the guarantee that a page below the first is served as the first. No ADR - the choice is a straightforward boundary clamp with no trade-off to record. No Known Defects row added: the defect is fixed by this slice rather than left standing, and that table records behavior that remains in the code. Non-numeric page values and pages beyond the last page stay out of scope per the prd-entry non_goals; if the implementer finds the fix cannot land without deciding one of them, raise a consultation-request rather than widening the slice. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

findings.description: The test's `FIRST_PAGE` (an `ArgumentMatcher<Pageable>` matching a zero-based page index) shares its exact name with `OwnerController.FIRST_PAGE` (an `int` holding the one-based page number 1). The two constants encode opposite ends of the very off-by-one convention this bug fix is about, so a reader moving between the production fix and its test sees the same identifier meaning two different things. Rename the test constant to something that names what it matches, e.g. `FIRST_PAGE_PAGEABLE` or `MATCHES_FIRST_PAGE`.
findings.fix: Rename `OwnerControllerTests.FIRST_PAGE` to a name that distinguishes it from `OwnerController.FIRST_PAGE`, e.g. `FIRST_PAGE_PAGEABLE`.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One module, one production method: three lines in OwnerController.processFindForm plus a constant, with the rest of the diff tests and two mechanical doc rows; no sensitive paths, no repository, template, or config touched.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is applied once at the handler boundary and the normalized value flows to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so the query and the rendered currentPage cannot diverge; no other use of the raw page value remains and no unrelated behavior shifts.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert the normalized zero-based Pageable via argThat and the currentPage model attribute rather than restating the code, and they would fail against the unfixed controller, where PageRequest.of(-1) throws; the last-name case pins that the search survives normalization.

reviewer_hedging.note: Both reviewers the low-risk plan dispatched approved in round two with empty findings and no recommendations; security-reviewer and doc-reviewer are null because the plan scoped them out, which is expected rather than silence.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, consultations, and build retries; the diff matches the design-block's primary paths exactly and the identical page-1 shape in VetController was deliberately left alone as a recorded non-goal.

rationale: The clamp normalizes once at the boundary, so query and displayed page stay in step, and the tests fail without it. Confirm and merge. Worth knowing, not blocking: VetController carries the same unclamped page-1 arithmetic, deferred by a recorded non-goal.
